How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide you can copy/paste into your terminal or script to hit the **Cisco Nexus Dashboard** REST API and pull the *speed* statistics for a specific interface. --- ### 1️⃣ What You Need | Item | How to Get It | |------|---------------| | **Dashboard IP** | `192.120.45.67` – already supplied | | **Endpoint Path** | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` | | **Query Parameters** |   - `fabricName=Network1`
  - `nodeId=12`
  - `podId=10`
  - `interfaceType=Ethernet`
  - `infoType=Speed` | | **Auth Method** | Most Nexus Dashboards use either **Basic Auth** (`username/password`) or a **Bearer Token** obtained via OAuth2 / SSO. Pick whichever matches your environment. | > ⚠️ If you’re unsure which auth scheme your instance uses, check the “Authentication” section under **Admin → System Settings → Security** in the UI. --- ### 2️⃣ Build the Full Request URL ```text https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo\ ?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed ``` *(Notice the backslash at the end of line 1 only helps readability when copying it as one continuous line.)* --- ### 3️⃣ Example Calls #### A) Using **cURL** ```bash curl -k \ # skip cert verification if self‑signed -u admin:admin123 \ # <-- replace with real creds "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?" \ --data-urlencode "fabricName=Network1" \ --data-urlencode "nodeId=12" \ --data-urlencode "podId=10" \ --data-urlencode "interfaceType=Ethernet" \ --data-urlencode "infoType=Speed" ``` If you have a bearer token: ```bash TOKEN="eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." curl -k \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?" \ --data-urlencode "fabricName=Network1" \ ...etc... ``` #### B) Using **Python + Requests** ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo" payload = { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "Ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } headers = {"Accept": "application/json"} # Option 1 – Basic Auth response = requests.get(BASE_URL, params=payload, headers=headers, auth=("admin", "admin123"), verify=False) # Option 2 – Bearer Token # response = requests.get( # BASE_URL, # params=payload, # headers={**headers, "Authorization": f"Bearer {YOUR_TOKEN_HERE}"}, # verify=False # ) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` > 👉 Set `verify=True` once you’ve installed a trusted CA certificate on the machine running this script. --- ### 4️⃣ Interpreting the Response A successful call will return JSON similar to: ```json { "fabricName":"Network1", "nodeId":12, "podId":10, "interfaceType":"Ethernet", "stats":{ "currentLinkSpeedMbps":1000, "maxSupportedSpeedGbps":10 } } ``` The exact keys depend on what the dashboard exposes for `infoType=Speed`. Look for fields such as `linkSpeed`, `operationalRate`, etc. --- ### 5️⃣ Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Symptom | Likely Cause | Quick Remedy | |---------|--------------|-------------| | `401 Unauthorized` | Wrong credentials/token | Double‑check username/password or refresh the JWT | | `404 Not Found` | Endpoint typo or wrong version | Verify the full path against the Swagger/OpenAPI docs | | SSL errors | Self‑signed cert not trusted | Add `--insecure/-k` flag or install the root cert | | Empty body | No matching data | Ensure the fabric/node/pod IDs exist and the interface really has speed stats | --- ### TL;DR Code Snippet (one liner) ```bash curl -k -u admin:admin123 "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` Replace `admin/admin123` with your own credentials or switch to a bearer header if required. Happy querying! 🚀
